topStories.headline: Valkyries Bring the WNBA Finals to Mission Bay — and a Crowd-Control Challenge
topStories.dek: The Golden State Valkyries host the Atlanta Dream at Chase Center in Games 1 and 2 of the 2026 WNBA Finals this week, their first-ever championship appearance in just their second season.
topStories.body:
Mission Bay's Chase Center becomes the center of the WNBA universe this week as the Golden State Valkyries host Games 1 and 2 of the 2026 WNBA Finals against the Atlanta Dream. Game 1 tips off Saturday at 12:30 p.m. PT on NBC, with Game 2 set for Monday, Oct. 19 at 5 p.m. The Valkyries reached the Finals after sweeping the defending-champion Las Vegas Aces 3–0 in the semifinals, earning the franchise its first Finals appearance in only its second season.

The stakes are high on both sides: the Dream, featuring WNBA star Angel Reese, have also never won a championship. The Valkyries, who led the WNBA in home attendance this season and hold homecourt advantage throughout the series, enter the Finals as the No. 2 seed. If the series extends, Games 5 and 7 would return to Chase Center on Oct. 26 and Oct. 31, respectively.

For neighbors, the games bring both excitement and logistical headaches. Game 1 coincides with the Bay Area Science Festival just one block away at UCSF's Koret Quad — both venues sit along the Third Street transit corridor and are urging visitors to leave their cars behind. Tickets for Games 1 and 2 sold out within minutes of going on sale Oct. 12, with resale prices starting around $300 and select VIP seats listed above $6,000.

topStories.headline: SoMa Leads City in Office Absorption as AI Firms Swap Starter Suites for Full Buildings
topStories.dek: Three of Q3's six largest office leases in San Francisco landed in South of Market, where AI and tech companies including Brex and Cognition are trading compact starter offices for vastly larger spaces — raising a new question about who fills the suites they leave behind.
topStories.body:
South of Market outpaced every other San Francisco submarket in Q3 office absorption, according to CBRE's third-quarter 2026 San Francisco office report released this week. Three of the quarter's six leases of 100,000 square feet or more landed in SoMa, absorbing a total of 484,000 square feet as tech tenants filled furnished, Class A blocks vacated earlier in the pandemic cycle.

The defining illustration of the trend is the paired story of Brex and Cognition. Brex signed a full-building, near-decade lease at 270 Brannan Street — the entire 200,000-square-foot building — after having previously leased only a portion of it. Simultaneously, AI firm Cognition signed a 182,054-square-foot sublease at 333 Brannan Street. Between them, the two companies traded roughly 41,000 square feet of starter space for nearly 380,000 square feet of SoMa real estate. CBRE's Q3 report found that nearly half of the city's 8.4 million square feet of current tenant demand is expansion-driven.

The broader numbers tell an improving story for SoMa, even as the direct vacancy rate there still sits at 29.5 percent, according to Kidder Mathews Q3 data. The SF Examiner reported this week that citywide, AI and tech startups drove 1.3 million square feet of positive net absorption in Q3, and that if the trend holds, 2026 would finish with the highest annual net absorption total on record. SoMa's draw is partly logistical: large, furnished Class A blocks sitting vacant and move-in ready attracted tenants who might previously have looked to the South Financial District. With no remaining large blocks in Mission Bay, CBRE data shows demand is now spilling into SoMa, Mid-Market, and Rincon/South Beach.

topStories.headline: Prologis Kicks Off Environmental Review for Massive Caltrain Railyards Redevelopment at 4th and King
topStories.dek: The San Francisco Planning Department held a public scoping meeting on October 14 to launch the environmental review process for a proposed 18.6-acre mixed-use development around the Caltrain station at 700 4th Street in SoMa — one of the largest single projects ever proposed in the city.
topStories.body:
San Francisco's Planning Department convened a public meeting on October 14 to formally begin the CEQA environmental review process for the Caltrain Railyards redevelopment at approximately 700 4th Street in SoMa. The meeting marked the issuance of a Notice of Preparation for the Draft Environmental Impact Report, giving the public a formal opportunity to submit comments that will shape the scope of the analysis.

Prologis, the world's largest industrial real estate company and the project's sponsor, has proposed redeveloping 18.6 acres encompassing the existing San Francisco Caltrain Station, railroad tracks, platforms, and maintenance areas. The master plan calls for housing, commercial offices, institutional space, retail, parking, and open space, along with full replacement and modernization of the station itself. A central planning question remains unresolved: whether the tracks will remain at-grade or be buried below ground — a decision that could add years and significant cost to the timeline.

Two development scenarios are currently under review. The maximum commercial scenario would yield 5.6 million square feet of commercial space and 1,765 residential units. The maximum residential alternative would deliver 5,834 units and 1.59 million square feet of office space. At full buildout, Prologis has described constructing between 7 and 8 million square feet total. The project also envisions serving as a gateway to the California High-Speed Rail network via a connection to the Salesforce Transit Center. A construction schedule filed earlier this year estimates 12 to 13 years to completion depending on the track alignment chosen.

moreNews.headline: SoMa's Newest Climbing Gym Opens on Folsom Street — With Lower Prices Than the Competition
moreNews.body: California Climbing Collective opened its doors on October 11 at 1264 Folsom Street in SoMa, capping more than three years of planning and buildout after owners Summer Bombard and Radu Popescu signed the lease in summer 2023. The opening celebration included free climbs, a DJ, and stick-and-poke tattoos. The independent bouldering gym features over 4,000 square feet of climbing terrain with walls reaching about 16 feet, and a spray wall used for training. Memberships are priced at $79 per month; day passes — available starting in November — will run $25, substantially below other Bay Area climbing gyms. Current hours are 3–10 p.m. Monday through Friday and 11 a.m.–8 p.m. on weekends, with extended morning hours planned for December.

moreNews.headline: Developer Files Permits for 45-Story, 528-Unit Tower at SoMa Car Wash Site
moreNews.body: Chicago-based Manna Capital filed preliminary permits on October 7 with the San Francisco Planning Department for a 479-foot, 45-story residential skyscraper at 1601 Mission Street — the site currently occupied by the Tower Car Wash near South Van Ness Avenue. The 633,600-square-foot project, designed by Solomon Cordwell Buenz, would deliver 528 rental apartments including 80 affordable units (40 for very low-income households, 40 for moderate-income) and a 900-square-foot ground-floor retail space. Amenities planned for the tower include a rooftop pool, spa, golf simulator, yoga studio, and co-working lounge. The proposal, which invokes the State Density Bonus and AB 1287 to more than double what was previously approved for the site, estimates construction costs of approximately $312 million. Nothing has been approved; the application is listed as submitted in city planning records.
